topic: what a Friday release checklist really needs

grades.notes:
coverage: 5 atoms across 4 types (number x2, mechanism, limit, object): the risk, the answer, the form, the outcome
specificity: each atom carries a figure or a named thing: 70%, 5 to 9 items, 19 items in three pauses of 7, 7 and 5, 1.5% to 0.8% in 8 hospitals
sourced: every row names a published work: the Google SRE book introduction, Gawande ch. 6, the WHO checklist, Haynes et al. NEJM 2009
surprise: atom 4 is not about software at all: a surgical checklist built around three stops, which a release list can borrow

novelty: operator 2 (the ratio) turns atom 5's 1.5% and 0.8% into 15 and 8 in a thousand; the two earlier pieces used the form and the 70% share
truth: 1.5% to 0.8% across 8 hospitals is Haynes et al., NEJM 2009; 15 and 8 per 1,000 is the same figure, not sharpened beyond it
relevance: the Friday list borrows the three stops; the ratio is the evidence that a short paused list changes an outcome
intrigue: a drop to about half from three pauses invites the question of what the pauses did, which the post answers
tone: plain; it reports a surgical result and says only that the pause can be borrowed, not that releases will halve outages

coherence: timetable lends a run of stops across; the sequence layout reads the surgical stops in order and ends on the ratio as the last step
feasibility: one page, local handnote faces, own warm palette from palette.py, the drawing is two runs of three stops, no picture needed
